originalTitle: Elon Musk's Tesla posts cash burn as capex surges on AI, robotaxi push
simplifiedContent: Tesla, a car company owned by Elon Musk, spent a lot of money in the last quarter, which means it didn't have as much cash as it would have liked. This happened because the company is investing heavily in new technologies like artificial intelligence and self-driving taxis. Even though Tesla sold more cars than expected and its energy storage business did well, it still lost $1.1 billion in cash. This is important because investors are watching to see if Tesla can grow in areas like self-driving cars, since the regular car market is getting more competitive. Investors are paying close attention to this because they want to know if Tesla's big spending will pay off in the long run.

originalTitle: Google quarterly cloud revenue growth beats expectations
simplifiedContent: Google recently reported that its cloud business is growing very quickly, with revenue increasing by 82% from the same time last year. This is good news for the company, especially since it helps make up for the money they're spending on artificial intelligence (AI) projects. The cloud business is doing well because many large companies want to use Google's AI services. Google's search business is also doing well, and is attracting more advertisers who want to use its AI features. This growth is important because it shows that Google's investments in AI are paying off, even if some of its own AI projects are taking longer than expected.

originalTitle: US stocks today: S&P 500, Nasdaq close lower amid mixed show by tech stocks ahead of earnings
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, which are like scorecards for the US stock market, ended the day lower. This is because some technology stocks, like software companies, didn't do well, while others, like chip makers, did better. Investors are being careful because some big companies, like Alphabet and Tesla, are about to report how they've been doing, and this can affect the market. The price of oil is also going up, and there are worries about global tensions, which is making the market a bit unpredictable. Overall, this is making investors a bit nervous, even though some people are feeling optimistic about new technologies.

originalTitle: Yen Rebound Ebbs After Brief Rally on Outlook for BOJ Rate Hikes
simplifiedContent: The value of the Japanese yen recently went down to its lowest point in a long time, with one dollar being able to buy more than 163 yen. However, the yen then regained some of its value in a volatile trading session. This happened because some people think the Bank of Japan might raise interest rates faster than expected. The yen's value went up a bit because of this possibility, but it's still not back to where it was before. This matters because changes in the yen's value can affect investments and the economy.

originalTitle: Two-year yields hit 17-month high on oil surge, Fed fears
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: the interest rate on a type of US government bond (called a 2-year Treasury) has reached its highest point in 17 months. This change is likely because of two main reasons: the recent increase in oil prices and concerns about what the Federal Reserve (the US central bank) will do next. When oil prices surge, it can cause inflation to rise, which might lead the Fed to raise interest rates to control it. As a result, investors are selling their existing bonds with lower interest rates, which drives up the yield on new bonds. This matters because it can affect the overall direction of the stock market and the economy.

originalTitle: Gold firms to two-week peak on softer dollar, Fed outlook in focus
simplifiedContent: The price of gold has risen to its highest point in two weeks. This happened because the value of the US dollar decreased, making gold more attractive to buy. Investors are also waiting to see what the Federal Reserve (or "Fed") will do next, which is affecting the price of gold. The Fed's decisions can impact the economy and the value of the dollar, which in turn affects the price of gold. This matters because it can help investors decide whether to buy or sell gold, and how it might fit into their overall investment strategy.
